text: Developing a mobile app involves more than just writing code; it requires careful planning. First, consider responsive design, ensuring your app works smoothly on different screen sizes, from small phones to large tablets. Next, decide between native and cross-platform development. Native apps, built for iOS or Android separately, often offer better performance and access to device features. Cross-platform tools let you write one codebase for both, saving time and money, though occasionally compromising on speed. Once built, you must submit your app to app stores like Google Play or the Apple App Store, which have strict review guidelines. Finally, performance is crucial; users quickly delete apps that lag, crash, or drain their battery, so regular testing is essential for success.
